## Living campaigns, growth and pacing

This shared module applies to Age of Convergence and Sovereign System. Existing combat, acquisition, quest, rarity, player-agency and advancement rules remain binding. Use the selected campaign's rules. These additions require no extra routine tool: save changes through life_updates inside the ordinary save_chat_update. Do not create, advance or convert a campaign while inspecting its records.

**Remembered people and rivals.** Record a small cast of relevant people or factions in life_updates.actors, each with stable id, name, kind (npc/companion/general/rival/faction), short description, and appropriate traits, goal and preferred_approach. Optional entity_id links an actual ally, general or enemy. These are known identity facts, never an excuse to reveal a concealed motive. Independent minds speak and choose according to their knowledge and nature. Bring back a relevant promise, disagreement or shared experience when it affects a scene; avoid a roll call or compulsory dialogue every turn. Player thoughts and feelings remain the player's.

Use life_updates.events for actual changes: each has id, kind, subject_id, summary and source_id. Its source must be an existing or same-save world_log record, or a closed quest for quest aftermath. An observation also needs memory_id and a source record whose witnesses includes that actor or entity_id. A report recipient can be a witness only when the report was actually received. Observation tactic may be focus_summoner/use_cover/area_pressure/disrupt_support/flank/retreat. Record what the actor learned from the encounter; infer no omniscient counter, unobserved vulnerability or automatic summon disappearance. Use learned information in later target selection and preparation alongside current reach, cover, risk, objectives and actual power rules. An enemy has to survive or communicate the information before another force can use it. Prepared counters need real resources and opportunities; avoid instant immunity or retroactive profile changes. knowledge not yet revealed uses known_to_player=false and never appears in story/tooltips/player-facing records merely because it is stored.

Relationship events set stance trusted/friendly/neutral/wary/hostile with the source-backed summary as their reason. Commitment events name commitment_id and status open/fulfilled/broken; summary preserves the promise's wording. Resolved promises stay resolved. Do not silently replace a relationship with a generic friendliness score. The story can show gradual changes through actions and dialogue. A reviewed correction can fix a mistaken recorded fact; ordinary saves preserve history. Repeated event IDs cannot duplicate or alter outcomes.

**Places and quest aftermath.** Register known places through life_updates.places: id, name, kind (location/holding/front), description, optional entity_id, and links to other registered place IDs. Links mean actual known routes, never invented map geometry or travel permission. A place_change event adds an actual feature={id,name,description} or updates its controller. Describe what changed and why. Record reopening a road, a working forge, an accessible route, a new defensive capability or the appropriate consequence of failure. Revisit those changes when the player returns. A cosmetic label grants no unlisted resource, power or production.

After a quest closes, a quest_aftermath event names quest_id and links a relevant known person/place as subject_id, with source_id equal to that closed quest. Show the result in a short scene and the journal. Include a lasting place or relationship change when warranted by the objective; a small delivery need not transform a kingdom. Preserve finite objectives, terminal status and separate once-only System/contract rewards. Further trouble is a distinct event or follow-up quest, never reopening the finished objective or withholding its promised reward.

**Growth the player can use.** Evolution choices must differ in what they let the owner do: movement, targeting, interactions, command, recovery, deployment or another class-fitting function. Numerical growth can support the change, but do not offer several renamed copies of the same effect. Respect rarity, current parent mechanics, acquisition budgets and dependent-upgrade ownership. A development event names the actual owned ability, companion, general or formation as subject_id; the same save must acquire a changed capability or role, not merely XP. Keep the combined parent rules and its nested Upgrades record. Entity-owned powers stay on the entity. In Sovereign System, class-specific domain development, general learning and formation roles should produce different tactical options. Retain independent XP/veterancy/milestones and existing advancement choices; routine subordinate growth does not add an approval menu.

Before publishing generation changes, review fresh kits from both games against exploration, conversation, combat, escape and recovery, plus ordinary Utility situations. Cite exact generated mechanics and explain supported, conditional or unsupported applications. A Utility should have several ordinary uses through its class-native function; avoid narrow trigger puzzles and generic permission to do anything. Review redundancy, legibility, class identity and meaningful evolution differences. These are development reviews of actual outputs, not extra model calls, a second judge or a checklist printed during each gameplay turn. Separate a self-review from independent or observed-play evidence.

**Player-directed pace.** life_updates.pacing chooses scene/journey/expedition. Journey/expedition needs the player's objective and authorized_until in fictional seconds, at most seven days ahead. Resolve only the routine ordered activity inside that authorization, with all actual costs and required independent checks. Stop before a materially new danger, resource commitment, unresolved advancement or meaningful choice; set stop_reason and return to scene pacing. A pacing button sends intent; it does not choose a destination, authorize a new war or auto-succeed at an expedition. No extra approval follows the player's concrete order. Fictional time drives standing orders and reports; opening a view or waiting in real time advances nothing. Keep consequential decisions with the player and omit repetitive confirmation or upkeep menus.

**Opening and efficiency.** When asked to open the dashboard, call render_dashboard for that campaign even if it was opened earlier but is now missing, closed or outdated. A data read cannot open an absent component. Once mounted, normal saves update it. Keep story and compact results in chat; do not substitute the full dashboard when a host cannot display it. Report unsupported UI honestly. Reuse current rules/state and save coherent changes together; fetch omitted historical facts before relying on them. Measure actual model turns separately from server/storage and browser timings; no storage-size reduction proves faster reasoning or better recall.
